report.title: NIFTY & BEYOND
report.headline: Across the week of 31 August to 5 September 2026, Indian equities consolidated in a narrow 1.15% range as Nifty closed at 23,897.70. Underneath, domestic institutions mounted a record weekly buying offensive (+₹23,156 Cr), absorbing heavy FII cash liquidation (-₹5,612 Cr). Sector rotation favored Energy and Banking, while a single corporate announcement by UltraTech Cement into wires & cables repriced the entire industrial capital goods space.

Nifty 50 closed at 23,897.70 (-1.15% 1W), Sensex at 76,515.43 (-0.95% 1W), and Nifty Bank at 57,369.65 (-0.02% 1W), holding key structural support.

+₹23,156.26 Cr

⚡
Industry Disruption:

🏢
Tijori Operational Intel:
Realty standout Brigade launched 'Brigade Barcelona' (₹2,700 Cr GDV); Tijori metrics confirm ₹12,915/sqft realization, 30.87M sqft pipeline, and 76% hotel occupancy.
😌
Fear Gauge & Volatility:
India VIX fell to 10.62 — a six-week low (82nd percentile calm), with weekly put writers moving defensive lines up 300 points to 23,900 at the money.
Across the week of 31 August to 5 September 2026, Indian equities consolidated in a narrow 1.15% range as Nifty closed at 23,897.70. Underneath, domestic institutions mounted a record weekly buying offensive (+₹23,156 Cr), absorbing heavy FII cash liquidation (-₹5,612 Cr). Sector rotation favored Energy and Banking, while a single corporate announcement by UltraTech Cement into wires & cables repriced the entire industrial capital goods space.
Source — Global prices: MCX EOD & Bloomberg Weekly Spot Rates. Prices are indicative weekly EOD values.

§3
What's Unusual This Week
Domestic Buying at Record Weekly High (+₹23,156 Cr)
1.0 of 39.0
Domestic institutions executed a record weekly net cash purchase of ₹23,156 crore across 5 sessions — by far the largest weekly allocation in our 39-session database, absorbing 412% of FII cash liquidation (-₹5,612 Cr).
NIACL — +23.4% 1W Breakout on NSE IPO Anticipation
1.0 of 250.0
Surged 23.4% over the week to a 52-week high of ₹229.30 on 7.6x volume (RSI 78.7 overbought, ADX 39.6). Driven by market pricing in value unlock from its 1.42% corporate equity stake in the upcoming NSE IPO.
KEI Industries — -12.9% 1W Cable De-Rating (Tijori Industry Intel)
1.0 of 250.0
Plunged 12.9% over the week on 5.5x volume (-12.8% below 20SMA, RSI 34) alongside Polycab (-8.7% 1W) and RR Kabel (-15.5% 1W). Triggered by UltraTech Cement's aggressive ₹1,800 Cr entry into wires & cables ('Ultravolt' brand). Tijori data shows Finolex & KEI communication cable realizations at ₹2,204/km across 2.63M km annual sales; UltraTech's entrance threatens long-term pricing power.
HBL Engineering — 12.3x Weekly Volume Expansion
1.0 of 250.0
Recorded the highest weekly volume multiple at 12.3x normal volume for a modest 3.2% weekly price gain. Indicates massive institutional block transfers rather than retail momentum.
Tejas Networks — +11.6% 1W Rally on ₹1,537 Cr BSNL Order
3.0 of 250.0
Gained 11.6% over the week on 6x volume (+15.4% above 20SMA, RSI 72.3). Powered by TCS's ₹1,537 Cr LOI for BSNL 4G/5G Radio Access Network equipment supply. Tijori metrics highlight R&D reinvestment held at 5.63% of sales and 3.82x net sales per employee cost ratio.
Brigade Enterprises — +8.4% 1W Expansion on Tijori Operational Strength
5.0 of 250.0
Gained 8.4% over the week following the announcement of 'Brigade Barcelona' in Hyderabad Neopolis corridor (₹2,700 Cr GDV). Tijori operational metrics confirm strong fundamental backing: ₹12,915/sqft realization, 30.87M sqft area under construction, 76% hotel occupancy with ₹7,241 ADR (RevPAR ₹5,503), and 7.61% borrowing cost.
Solar Industries — Tijori Order Book Intel (145.5% of Sales)
2.0 of 250.0
Maintained institutional focus amid South Africa acquisition clarifications. Tijori metrics reveal bulk explosives realization of ₹47,340/MT across 5.88L tonnes annual volume, with defense & commercial order book standing at 145.5% of annual revenue.
Nifty Oil & Gas — 27-Point Weekly Breadth Swing
1.0 of 24.0
The share of Nifty Oil and Gas constituents above their 20-day average rose 27 percentage points over 5 sessions (best weekly sector performer at +1.08% 1W), as Brent crude held near $95 and refining margins firmed.
Nifty FMCG — 0% Stocks >20D SMA for 2 Consecutive Weeks
24.0 of 24.0
FMCG sector ended the week with zero of fifteen constituents trading above their 20-day SMA (-2.0% 1W, -7.34% 1M). Demonstrates a persistent structural drawdown in consumer staples.
India VIX — 10.62 Six-Week Low Compression
45.0 of 250.0
India VIX fell to 10.62 (82nd percentile calm) despite ongoing Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions, creating extreme volatility compression.
Ranked by weekly statistical unusualness against multi-week history.

Held steady at 6.50% with hawkish stance ('withdrawal of accommodation'). Minutes highlight inflation persistence concerns.

Traded at 6.94%, anchoring domestic borrowing costs as the risk-free rate.
Bank Credit vs Deposit Growth Gap (#3):
Credit growth ran at 14.2% YoY while deposit growth lagged at 10.8% YoY, maintaining margin pressure on banks and driving CD issuance.
Daily Systemic Liquidity (#2):
Net LAF operations maintained a comfortable ₹42,000 Cr liquidity surplus in the banking system.

Index of Industrial Production (#10) & Eight Core (#11):
Industrial output grew 4.8% YoY led by Capital Goods (+7.2%) and Electricity (+6.1%).
CPI Inflation Trajectory (#7):
Headline inflation moderated to 3.54% YoY, staying within RBI's 4.0% (+/- 2%) target band.

IMD Southwest Monsoon (#19):

$740.803 billion

Institutional Cash Flows (#25):
FPIs sold -₹5,612 Cr net cash over the week, which was heavily absorbed by record DII buying (+₹23,156 Cr).
AMFI Monthly SIP Inflows (#26):
Monthly SIP contributions hit a record ₹23,332 Cr, supplying a steady ₹1,100 Cr daily domestic liquidity cushion.
Merchandise Trade & CAD (#28, #29):
Trade deficit narrowed to $23.5Bn; Current Account Deficit remains comfortable at 1.1% of GDP.
Global Central Banks, Commodities & Yields (Top 50 Macro #38 – #50)
$95.23 Crude / 104.2 DXY
US Fed · DXY · Brent Crude · China PMI

US 10-Year Treasury yield eased 4 bps to 4.79% as markets priced in a September FOMC rate cut.
US Dollar Index DXY (#43):
DXY held around 104.20, keeping Asian currency volatility constrained.
Brent Crude & OPEC+ (#47, #48):
Brent firmed to $95.23/bbl on Hormuz transit friction and OPEC+ production caps.
China Manufacturing PMI (#49):
Caixin Manufacturing PMI ticked up to 50.4, supporting base metals prices (Aluminium +0.67% 1W).

Timing matters.
US markets close after India's. Wall Street figures reflect weekly closes — they provided the cue for Friday's open, and next week's US session is the cue for Monday. Brent, gold, silver and the rupee trade through Indian hours.
The transmission chain, named.
Over the week, global market signals traveled into India along three paths.
First
, into the open: US rate-hike fears eased Friday, Wall Street bounced, and Nifty futures moved from short buildup to short covering.
Second
, into currency: softer dollar expectations combined with record RBI reserves ($740.8Bn) allowed India to absorb $95 crude without currency depreciation.
Third
, into safe havens: gold (-1.86% 1W) and silver (-1.64% 1W) unwound safe-haven bids. Where the chain did
not
reach is domestic consumer breadth — 264 shares fell Friday, FMCG remained at 0% >20D, and Auto breadth dropped 46 points over 5 sessions.

Eight sectors moved enough in weekly breadth to flag. They split into a banking-and-energy group that is quietly strengthening and a manufacturing-and-defensive group that is deteriorating fast.
NIFTY IT
— worst breadth for a second consecutive session: 0.25 A/D, share above 20D SMA dropped 40 points in 3 sessions to 30%. Index down 1.88% over the week.
NIFTY HEALTHCARE
— breadth of 0.18, worse than IT. Share above 20D SMA at 25% after 20-point drop; index down 2.32% 1W.
NIFTY PSU BANK
— share above 20D SMA rose 25 points in 3 sessions to 50%, a clear positive rotation.
NIFTY CAPITAL GOODS
— dramatic reversal. Flipped from +14 to -12 on 5-day breadth due to UltraTech cable entry.
NIFTY REALTY
— profit taking after a vertical move. Down 0.90% Friday but up 18.74% over 3 months.
NIFTY AUTO
— most damaged sector. A/D 0.15, just 7% above 20D SMA, down 46 points of breadth in 5 sessions (-3.95% 1W).
NIFTY METAL
— best sector Friday (+1.07%), 53% above 20D SMA.
NIFTY FMCG
— second week with 0% of constituents above 20D SMA (-2.0% 1W, -7.34% 1M).

§8
Weekly Sector Rotation
Rotating in (Weekly)
Rotating out (Weekly)
The weekly rotation has sharpened into a simple macro thesis: money is moving into banks and energy, and out of manufacturing and defensives. Banking and Oil & Gas dominate weekly breadth gains; Auto, Consumer Durables, Healthcare, and IT dominate weekly breadth losses. That is a bet on domestic credit growth and high energy prices, funded by selling consumer and tech exposure.

§
How to Read This Report
The order matters more than the sections. Most readers open at the index level and stop there — which is the habit that makes a narrow market look healthy.
1
Start with weekly participation, not the index
Open §7. Which direction is the number of stocks above their 50-day average moving over the last 4 weeks? That is the market’s true direction of travel.
2
Then check the weekly index against it
If the Nifty was flat or mildly green while fewer stocks are above their 20-day average than last week, participation is falling inside a narrow market.
3
Read sector leadership across weekly timeframes
In §6b, compare each sector’s 1-week move against its 1-month and 3-month bars. A sector strong on all three is structural leadership.
4
Cross-check each sector’s weekly move against its breadth
A sector that rose this week but whose participation column is falling has a narrow move. §6b row next to §7 row is the comparison.
5
Go straight to the flagged weekly sectors
Read §7’s notable weekly flags and §9’s weekly scanner names together to identify institutional positioning.
6
Ask whether weekly money agrees with positioning
Compare §11 (cumulative weekly FII/DII net flows) with §13 (options put floor and call wall). Conviction shows when both point the same way.
